Gaal@Jdg.9.26-.description: Gaal, the son of Ebed, led a revolt against Abimelech, the ruler of Shechem, but was defeated and driven out of the city.
Gaal@Jdg.9.26-.name: Gaal

Gaash@Jos.24.30-1Ch.description: Gaash, a mountain in the region of Ephraim, was the burial place of Joshua and the homeland of two of David's mighty men.
Gaash@Jos.24.30-1Ch.name: Gaash

Gabbai@Neh.11.8.description: Gabbai was a Benjamite leader who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
Gabbai@Neh.11.8.name: Gabbai

Gabbatha@Jhn.19.13.description: Gabbatha, also known as the Stone Pavement, was the location in Jerusalem where Pontius Pilate sat in judgment over Jesus.
Gabbatha@Jhn.19.13.name: Gabbatha

Gabriel@Dan.8.16-Luk.description: Gabriel is an angel who appears in the Bible to deliver important messages from God, such as interpreting visions for Daniel (<ref="Dan.8.16; 9:21">Dan.8.16; 9:21</ref>) and announcing the births of John the Baptist and Jesus (<ref="Luke 1:19, 26">Luke 1:19, 26</ref>).
Gabriel@Dan.8.16-Luk.name: Gabriel

Gad@1Sa.22.5-2Ch.description: Gad was a prophet who advised King David and wrote a book of his acts.
Gad@1Sa.22.5-2Ch.name: Gad

Gad@Gen.30.11-Rev.description: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, descended from Gad, the son of Jacob, and known for their military prowess and settlement east of the Jordan River.
Gad@Gen.30.11-Rev.name: Gad

Gaddi@Num.13.11.description: Gaddi, the son of Susi, was the representative of the tribe of Manasseh among the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.
Gaddi@Num.13.11.name: Gaddi

Gaddiel@Num.13.10.description: Gaddiel, the son of Sodi, was the representative of the tribe of Zebulun among the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.
Gaddiel@Num.13.10.name: Gaddiel

Gadi@2Ki.15.14-.description: Gadi was the father of Menahem, who became king of Israel after assassinating Shallum.
Gadi@2Ki.15.14-.name: Gadi

Gaham@Gen.22.24.description: Gaham was one of the sons born to Nahor, Abraham's brother, and his concubine Reumah.
Gaham@Gen.22.24.name: Gaham

Gahar@Ezr.2.47-Neh.description: Gahar was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
Gahar@Ezr.2.47-Neh.name: Gahar

Gaius@3Jn.1.1.description: Gaius, the recipient of John's third epistle, was commended for his faithfulness to the truth and his hospitality to traveling missionaries.
Gaius@3Jn.1.1.name: Gaius

Gaius@Act.19.29.description: Gaius, a Macedonian and traveling companion of Paul, was seized along with Aristarchus during the riot in Ephesus.
Gaius@Act.19.29.name: Gaius

Gaius@Act.20.4.description: Gaius of Derbe accompanied Paul on his journey from Greece to Jerusalem, along with several others.
Gaius@Act.20.4.name: Gaius

Gaius@Rom.16.23-1Co.description: Gaius, a Corinthian believer baptized by Paul, hosted Paul and the whole church in his home.
Gaius@Rom.16.23-1Co.name: Gaius

Galal@1Ch.9.15.description: Galal, a Levite musician and descendant of Asaph, lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.
Galal@1Ch.9.15.name: Galal

Galal@1Ch.9.16-Neh.description: Galal, a Levite musician and descendant of Jeduthun, lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile and assisted in the temple service.
Galal@1Ch.9.16-Neh.name: Galal

Galatia@Act.16.6-1Pe.description: Galatia, a region in Asia Minor, was the recipient of Paul's epistle to the Galatians and was visited by Paul on his missionary journeys (<ref="Act.16.6; 18:23; 1Co.16.1; Galatians 1:2; 3:1; 6:18; 2Ti.4.10; 1Pe.1.1">Act.16.6; 18:23; 1Co.16.1; Galatians 1:2; 3:1; 6:18; 2Ti.4.10; 1Pe.1.1</ref>).
Galatia@Act.16.6-1Pe.name: Galatia

Galilee@Jos.12.23-Act.description: Galilee, a region in northern Israel, was a significant location in Jesus' life and ministry, as well as the homeland of many of his disciples.
Galilee@Jos.12.23-Act.name: Galilee

Gallim@1Sa.25.44-Isa.description: Gallim, a town in Benjamin, was the home of Paltiel, Michal's husband, and is mentioned in a prophecy of Isaiah.
Gallim@1Sa.25.44-Isa.name: Gallim

Gallio@Act.18.12-.description: Gallio, the Roman proconsul of Achaia, refused to judge Paul when the Jews brought charges against him in Corinth.
Gallio@Act.18.12-.name: Gallio

Gamad@Ezk.27.11.description: The Gamad were a people group mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy as defenders of the towers of Tyre.
Gamad@Ezk.27.11.name: Gamad

Gamaliel@Act.5.34-.description: Gamaliel, a respected Pharisee and teacher of the law, was Paul's mentor and advised the Sanhedrin to be cautious in their treatment of the apostles.
Gamaliel@Act.5.34-.name: Gamaliel

Gamaliel@Num.1.10-.description: Gamaliel, the son of Pedahzur, was the leader of the tribe of Manasseh during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.
Gamaliel@Num.1.10-.name: Gamaliel

Gamul@1Ch.24.17.description: Gamul was the head of the twenty-second priestly division organized during King David's reign.
Gamul@1Ch.24.17.name: Gamul

Gareb@2Sa.23.38-1Ch.description: Gareb the Ithrite was one of David's mighty warriors, known for his military prowess.
Gareb@2Sa.23.38-1Ch.name: Gareb

Gareb@Jer.31.39.description: Gareb, a hill mentioned in <ref="Jeremiah 31:39">Jeremiah 31:39</ref>, was located near Jerusalem and was to be included within the city's future boundaries.
Gareb@Jer.31.39.name: Gareb

Garmites@1Ch.4.19.description: The Garmite town of Keilah was founded by a son of Hodiah of Judah.
Garmites@1Ch.4.19.name: Garmites

Gatam@Gen.36.11-1Ch.description: Gatam was a son of Eliphaz, grandson of Esau, and one of the chiefs of Edom.
Gatam@Gen.36.11-1Ch.name: Gatam

Gath-hepher@Jos.19.13-2Ki.description: Gath-hepher, a town in the territory of Zebulun, was the hometown of the prophet Jonah.
Gath-hepher@Jos.19.13-2Ki.name: Gath-hepher

Gath-rimmon@Jos.19.45-1Ch.description: Gath-rimmon, a Levitical city, was allotted to the Kohathite Levites within the territories of Dan and Manasseh.
Gath-rimmon@Jos.19.45-1Ch.name: Gath-rimmon

Gath@Jos.11.22-Mic.description: Gath, one of the five major Philistine cities, was the hometown of Goliath and a place of refuge for David during his flight from Saul.
Gath@Jos.11.22-Mic.name: Gath

Gaza@Gen.10.19-Act.description: Gaza, one of the five major Philistine cities, was the site of Samson's exploits and a place visited by Philip the evangelist in the early church.
Gaza@Gen.10.19-Act.name: Gaza

Gazez@1Ch.2.46a.description: Gazez was a son of Caleb and his concubine Ephah, born after Haran.
Gazez@1Ch.2.46a.name: Gazez

Gazez@1Ch.2.46b.description: Gazez was a grandson of Caleb, born to Haran's son Gazez.
Gazez@1Ch.2.46b.name: Gazez

Gazzam@Ezr.2.48-Neh.description: Gazzam was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
Gazzam@Ezr.2.48-Neh.name: Gazzam

Ge-harashim@1Ch.4.14-Neh.description: Ge-harashim, the Valley of Craftsmen, was inhabited by some Benjamites after the return from the Babylonian exile.
Ge-harashim@1Ch.4.14-Neh.name: Ge-harashim

Geba@Jos.18.24-Zec.description: Geba, a Levitical city in the territory of Benjamin, was located on the northern border of the kingdom of Judah (<ref="Joshua 18:24; 1Ki.15.22">Joshua 18:24; 1Ki.15.22</ref>).
Geba@Jos.18.24-Zec.name: Geba

Gebal@Jos.13.5-Ezk.description: Gebal, a Phoenician city known for its skilled builders, was allied against Israel and provided materials for Solomon's temple.
Gebal@Jos.13.5-Ezk.name: Gebal

Geber@1Ki.4.19.description: Geber, the son of Uri, was one of the twelve district governors appointed by King Solomon to provide food for the royal household.
Geber@1Ki.4.19.name: Geber

Gebim@Isa.10.31.description: Gebim, a town in Benjamin, is mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy describing the advance of the Assyrian army towards Jerusalem.
Gebim@Isa.10.31.name: Gebim

Gedaliah@1Ch.25.3-.description: Gedaliah, a son of Jeduthun, was one of the temple musicians appointed by King David to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals.
Gedaliah@1Ch.25.3-.name: Gedaliah

Gedaliah@2Ki.25.22-Jer.description: Gedaliah, appointed governor of Judah by the Babylonians after the fall of Jerusalem, was assassinated by Ishmael, leading to the flight of the remaining Jews to Egypt.
Gedaliah@2Ki.25.22-Jer.name: Gedaliah

Gedaliah@Ezr.10.18.description: Gedaliah, a priest, was among those who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile and pledged to put them away.
Gedaliah@Ezr.10.18.name: Gedaliah

Gedaliah@Jer.38.1.description: Gedaliah, the son of Pashhur, was one of the officials who heard Jeremiah's message and urged King Zedekiah to put him to death.
Gedaliah@Jer.38.1.name: Gedaliah

Gedaliah@Zep.1.1.description: Gedaliah was the grandfather of the prophet Zephaniah, who prophesied during the reign of King Josiah of Judah.
Gedaliah@Zep.1.1.name: Gedaliah

Gederah@Jos.15.36-1Ch.description: Gederah, a town in Judah, was the home of Baal-hanan, one of David's overseers, and Jozabad, one of his mighty men.
Gederah@Jos.15.36-1Ch.name: Gederah

Gederoth@Jos.15.41-2Ch.description: Gederoth, a town in Judah, was captured by the Philistines during the reign of King Ahaz.
Gederoth@Jos.15.41-2Ch.name: Gederoth

Gederothaim@Jos.15.36.description: Gederothaim, a town in Judah, is mentioned in the list of cities allotted to the tribe of Judah.
Gederothaim@Jos.15.36.name: Gederothaim

Gedor@1Ch.4.39.description: Gedor, a region where some Simeonites went to find pasture for their flocks during the reign of King Hezekiah.
Gedor@1Ch.4.39.name: Gedor

Gedor@1Ch.8.31-.description: Gedor was a son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel'), the  father (ie re-founder) of Gibeon, and an ancestor of King Saul.
Gedor@1Ch.8.31-.name: Gedor

Gedor@Jos.12.13-1Ch.description: Gedor (or Geder), a town in the hill country of Judah, was the home of several members of Judahite clans.
Gedor@Jos.12.13-1Ch.name: Gedor

Gehazi@2Ki.4.12-.description: Gehazi, the servant of the prophet Elisha, was punished with leprosy for his greed and deceit in the matter of Naaman's healing.
Gehazi@2Ki.4.12-.name: Gehazi

Gemalli@Num.13.12.description: Gemalli was the father of Ammiel, who represented the tribe of Dan as one of the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.
Gemalli@Num.13.12.name: Gemalli

Gemariah@Jer.29.3.description: Gemariah, the son of Hilkiah, was a messenger sent by King Zedekiah of Judah to deliver a letter to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.
Gemariah@Jer.29.3.name: Gemariah

Gemariah@Jer.36.10-.description: Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, was an official during King Jehoiakim's reign who opposed the burning of Jeremiah's scroll.
Gemariah@Jer.36.10-.name: Gemariah

Gennesaret@Mat.14.34-Luk.description: Gennesaret, a fertile plain on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee, was the location of several events in Jesus' ministry.
Gennesaret@Mat.14.34-Luk.name: Gennesaret

Genubath@1Ki.11.20.description: Genubath was the son of Hadad the Edomite and was raised in Pharaoh's palace alongside the Pharaoh's own children.
Genubath@1Ki.11.20.name: Genubath

Gera@1Ch.8.3.description: Gera was a son of Bela and a grandson of Benjamin.
Gera@1Ch.8.3.name: Gera

Gera@1Ch.8.7.description: Gera (or Heglam) was a son of Ehud, a Benjamite, and was among those who were carried into exile.
Gera@1Ch.8.7.name: Gera

Gera@2Sa.16.5-1Ki.description: Gera was a Benjamite who cursed David during Absalom's rebellion but later sought forgiveness when David returned to Jerusalem.
Gera@2Sa.16.5-1Ki.name: Gera

Gera@Gen.46.21-1Ch.description: Gera was a descendant of Benjamin and an ancestor of Ehud, a left-handed judge who delivered Israel from Moabite oppression.
Gera@Gen.46.21-1Ch.name: Gera

Gerar@Gen.10.19-2Ch.description: Gerar, a Philistine city, was the location of Abraham and Isaac's encounters with Abimelech and the site of a battle during King Asa's reign.
Gerar@Gen.10.19-2Ch.name: Gerar

Gerasa@Mat.8.28-Luk.description: Gerasa (or Gadara), a region southeast of the Sea of Galilee, was the location where Jesus healed a demon-possessed man.
Gerasa@Mat.8.28-Luk.name: Gerasa

Gerizim_Mount@Deu.11.29-Jdg.description: Mount Gerizim, a mountain in Samaria, was designated as the site for pronouncing blessings and was the location of Jotham's parable to the men of Shechem.
Gerizim_Mount@Deu.11.29-Jdg.name: Gerizim_Mount

Gershom@Exo.2.22-1Ch.description: Gershom was the firstborn son of Moses and Zipporah, and his descendant Jonathan served as a priest for the idolatrous Danites.
Gershom@Exo.2.22-1Ch.name: Gershom

Gershom@Ezr.8.2.description: Gershom, a descendant of Phinehas, was among the men who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra after the Babylonian exile.
Gershom@Ezr.8.2.name: Gershom

Gershon@Gen.46.11-2Ch.description: Gershon was the firstborn son of Levi and the ancestor of the Gershonite Levites, who were responsible for the tabernacle curtains, coverings, and related duties.
Gershon@Gen.46.11-2Ch.name: Gershon

Geruth_Chimham@Jer.41.17.description: Geruth Chimham, a lodging place near Bethlehem, served as a temporary refuge for Johanan and his group after the murder of Gedaliah.
Geruth_Chimham@Jer.41.17.name: Geruth_Chimham

Geshan@1Ch.2.47.description: Geshan was a son of Jahdai, a wife of Caleb, from the tribe of Judah.
Geshan@1Ch.2.47.name: Geshan

Geshem@Neh.2.19-.description: Geshem the Arab, along with Sanballat and Tobiah, opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem and tried to intimidate and discourage him.
Geshem@Neh.2.19-.name: Geshem

Geshur@Deu.3.14-1Ch.description: Geshur, an Aramean kingdom ruled by Talmai, was the homeland of David's wife Maacah and a refuge for Absalom after he murdered his half-brother Amnon.
Geshur@Deu.3.14-1Ch.name: Geshur

Gether@Gen.10.23-1Ch.description: Gether was a son of Aram and a grandson of Shem, mentioned in the genealogies of the Table of Nations.
Gether@Gen.10.23-1Ch.name: Gether

Gethsemane@Mat.26.36-Mrk.description: Gethsemane, a garden at the Mount of Olives, was the site where Jesus prayed and was arrested before his crucifixion.
Gethsemane@Mat.26.36-Mrk.name: Gethsemane

Geuel@Num.13.15.description: Geuel, the son of Machi, was the representative of the tribe of Gad among the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore Canaan.
Geuel@Num.13.15.name: Geuel

Giah@2Sa.2.24.description: Giah was a place near Gibeon where Joab and Abishai pursued Abner after the battle at the pool of Gibeon.
Giah@2Sa.2.24.name: Giah

Gibbethon@Jos.19.44-1Ki.description: Gibbethon, a Levitical city in the territory of Dan, was the site of conflict during the reigns of Nadab and Baasha (<ref="Joshua 19:44; 21:23; 1Ki.15.27; 16:15, 17">Joshua 19:44; 21:23; 1Ki.15.27; 16:15, 17</ref>).
Gibbethon@Jos.19.44-1Ki.name: Gibbethon

Gibea@1Ch.2.49.description: Gibea, with Machbenah, daughters or cities founded by Sheva.
Gibea@1Ch.2.49.name: Gibea

Gibeah@Jos.15.57-2Ch.description: Gibeah, a town in the hill country of Judah, was the hometown of Maacah, the mother of King Abijah (<ref="Joshua 15:57; 2Ch.13.2">Joshua 15:57; 2Ch.13.2</ref>).
Gibeah@Jos.15.57-2Ch.name: Gibeah

Gibeah@Jos.18.28-Hos.description: Gibeah, a city of Benjamin, was the hometown of Saul and the site of infamous atrocities during the time of the judges (<ref="Judges 19-20; 1Sa.10.5, 10, 26; 15:34; Hosea 9:9; 10:9">Judges 19-20; 1Sa.10.5, 10, 26; 15:34; Hosea 9:9; 10:9</ref>).
Gibeah@Jos.18.28-Hos.name: Gibeah

Gibeath-elohim@1Sa.10.5.description: Gibeath-elohim, meaning "Hill of God," was a place near Gibeah where a garrison of Philistines was located (<ref="1Sa.10.5">1Sa.10.5</ref>).
Gibeath-elohim@1Sa.10.5.name: Gibeath-elohim

Gibeon@Jos.9.3-Ezk.description: Gibeon was a prominent Hivite city that deceived Joshua into making a peace treaty, and later became a Levitical city and site of worship.
Gibeon@Jos.9.3-Ezk.name: Gibeon

Giddalti@1Ch.25.4-.description: Giddalti was one of the sons of Heman, appointed by King David as a temple musician to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals.
Giddalti@1Ch.25.4-.name: Giddalti

Giddel@Ezr.2.47-Neh.description: Giddel was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
Giddel@Ezr.2.47-Neh.name: Giddel

Giddel@Ezr.2.56-Neh.description: Giddel was an ancestor of a group of Solomon's servants who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.
Giddel@Ezr.2.56-Neh.name: Giddel

Gideon@Jdg.6.11-Heb.description: Gideon, also called Jerubbaal or Jerubbesheth, was a judge of Israel who, with God's help, defeated the Midianites and delivered Israel from oppression.
Gideon@Jdg.6.11-Heb.name: Gideon

Gideoni@Num.1.11-.description: Gideoni, the son of Abidan, was the leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.
Gideoni@Num.1.11-.name: Gideoni

Gidom@Jdg.20.45.description: Gidom was a place near Gibeah where the Benjamites were pursued and defeated during the Benjamite War (<ref="Judges 20:45">Judges 20:45</ref>).
Gidom@Jdg.20.45.name: Gidom

Gihon@Gen.2.13-2Ch.description: Gihon refers to both a river of Eden (<ref="Genesis 2:13">Genesis 2:13</ref>) and a spring near Jerusalem (<ref="1Ki.1.33, 38, 45; 2Ch.32.30; 33:14">1Ki.1.33, 38, 45; 2Ch.32.30; 33:14</ref>).
Gihon@Gen.2.13-2Ch.name: Gihon

Gilalai@Neh.12.36.description: Gilalai was a priest and musician who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.
Gilalai@Neh.12.36.name: Gilalai

Gilboa@1Sa.28.4-2Sa.description: Mount Gilboa was the site of a battle where Saul and his sons were killed by the Philistines (<ref="1Sa.28.4; 2Sa.1.21; 21:12">1Sa.28.4; 2Sa.1.21; 21:12</ref>).
Gilboa@1Sa.28.4-2Sa.name: Gilboa

Gilboa_Mount@Jdg.7.3-1Ch.description: Mount Gilboa was the site where Saul and his sons were killed in battle against the Philistines (<ref="1Sa.31.1, 8; 2Sa.1.6; 1Ch.10.1, 8; Judges 7:3">1Sa.31.1, 8; 2Sa.1.6; 1Ch.10.1, 8; Judges 7:3</ref>).
Gilboa_Mount@Jdg.7.3-1Ch.name: Gilboa_Mount

Gilead@1Ch.5.14.description: Gilead, a descendant of Manasseh, was the son of Michael and the father of Jaroah, as recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Gad.
Gilead@1Ch.5.14.name: Gilead

Gilead@Gen.31.21-Zec.description: Gilead refers to a mountainous region east of the Jordan River, as well as being a personal name for several individuals in the Old Testament.
Gilead@Gen.31.21-Zec.name: Gilead

Gilead@Jdg.11.1-.description: Gilead was the father of Jephthah, a mighty warrior and judge of Israel who delivered the Israelites from the Ammonites.
Gilead@Jdg.11.1-.name: Gilead

Gilead@Num.26.29-1Ch.description: Gilead was the son of Machir, grandson of Manasseh, and father of six sons who became the heads of Gileadite clans.
Gilead@Num.26.29-1Ch.name: Gilead

Gilgal@2Ki.2.1-.description: Gilgal, a place associated with the prophets Elijah and Elisha, was the starting point of Elijah's final journey and the location of a prophetic community (<ref="2Ki.2.1; 4:38">2Ki.2.1; 4:38</ref>).
Gilgal@2Ki.2.1-.name: Gilgal

Gilgal@Deu.11.30-Mic.description: Gilgal, also known as Geliloth, Beth-gilgal, or Gibeath-haaraloth, was a significant site during Israel's early history in Canaan, serving as a base for Joshua and a place of worship (<ref="Deu.11.30; Joshua 4:19-20; 5:3,9-10; 14:6; Judges 2:1; 11:14-15; 15:12-33; Hosea 9:15">Deu.11.30; Joshua 4:19-20; 5:3,9-10; 14:6; Judges 2:1; 11:14-15; 15:12-33; Hosea 9:15</ref>).
Gilgal@Deu.11.30-Mic.name: Gilgal

Giloh@Jos.15.51-2Sa.description: Giloh, also known as Gilo, was a city in Judah and the hometown of Ahithophel, David's counselor who later conspired with Absalom (<ref="Joshua 15:51; 2Sa.15.12; 23:34">Joshua 15:51; 2Sa.15.12; 23:34</ref>).
Giloh@Jos.15.51-2Sa.name: Giloh

Gimzo@2Ch.28.18.description: Gimzo was a city in the plain of Judah that was captured by the Philistines during the reign of Ahaz (<ref="2Ch.28.18">2Ch.28.18</ref>).
Gimzo@2Ch.28.18.name: Gimzo

Ginath@1Ki.16.21-.description: Ginath was the father of Tibni, who contended with Omri for the throne of Israel.
Ginath@1Ki.16.21-.name: Ginath

Ginnethon@Neh.10.6-.description: Ginnethon, a priest, was among those who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's reforms.
Ginnethon@Neh.10.6-.name: Ginnethon

Girgashites@Gen.10.16-Neh.description: The Girgashites were one of the Canaanite groups inhabiting the land promised to Abraham's descendants.
Girgashites@Gen.10.16-Neh.name: Girgashites

Girzites@1Sa.27.8.description: The Girzites were a people group David raided during his time living in Philistine territory.
Girzites@1Sa.27.8.name: Girzites

Gishpa@Neh.11.21.description: Gishpa was an overseer of the temple servants (Nethinim) during Nehemiah's time.
Gishpa@Neh.11.21.name: Gishpa

Gittaim@2Sa.4.3-Neh.description: Gittaim was a town where the Beerothites fled and was later inhabited by the Benjamites after the Babylonian exile.
Gittaim@2Sa.4.3-Neh.name: Gittaim

Gittith@Psa.8.1-.description: Gittith, mentioned in the superscriptions of Psalms 8, 81, and 84, is a musical term of uncertain meaning, possibly referring to a musical instrument, a tune, or a style associated with the city of Gath.
Gittith@Psa.8.1-.name: Gittith

Gizonites@1Ch.11.34.description: The Gizonites are mentioned in <ref="1Ch.11.34">1Ch.11.34</ref> without any additional context.
Gizonites@1Ch.11.34.name: Gizonites

Goah@Jer.31.39.description: Goah was a place near Jerusalem, mentioned in the context of a prophetic description of the city's future restoration (<ref="Jeremiah 31:39">Jeremiah 31:39</ref>).
Goah@Jer.31.39.name: Goah

Gog@1Ch.5.4.description: Gog, a descendant of Reuben, is mentioned in the genealogy of Reuben in <ref="1Ch.5.4">1Ch.5.4</ref>.
Gog@1Ch.5.4.name: Gog

Gog@Ezk.38.2-Rev.description: Gog is mentioned in the prophetic books of Ezekiel and Revelation as a symbolic enemy of God's people who will be defeated in the end times (<ref="Ezk.38.2, 3, 14, 16, 18; 39:1, 11; Revelation 20:8">Ezk.38.2, 3, 14, 16, 18; 39:1, 11; Revelation 20:8</ref>).
Gog@Ezk.38.2-Rev.name: Gog

Goiim@Gen.14.1-Jos.description: Tidal, king of Goiim (nations), was one of the kings who fought alongside Chedorlaomer in Genesis 14.
Goiim@Gen.14.1-Jos.name: Goiim

Golan@Deu.4.43-1Ch.description: Golan was a city of refuge in Bashan, allotted to the Levites of the family of Gershon and located in the territory of the half-tribe of Manasseh (<ref="Deu.4.43; Joshua 20:8; 21:27; 1Ch.6.71">Deu.4.43; Joshua 20:8; 21:27; 1Ch.6.71</ref>).
Golan@Deu.4.43-1Ch.name: Golan

Golgotha@Mat.27.33-Jhn.description: Golgotha, also known as the Place of a Skull, was the site outside Jerusalem where Jesus was crucified (<ref="Matthew 27:33; Mrk.15.22; Luke 23:33; Jhn.19.17">Matthew 27:33; Mrk.15.22; Luke 23:33; Jhn.19.17</ref>).
Golgotha@Mat.27.33-Jhn.name: Golgotha

Goliath@1Sa.17.4-1Ch.description: Goliath was the Philistine champion from Gath who was defeated by David in a battle.
Goliath@1Sa.17.4-1Ch.name: Goliath

Gomer@Gen.10.2-Ezk.description: Gomer, a son of Japheth, was the father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah, as listed in the Table of Nations.
Gomer@Gen.10.2-Ezk.name: Gomer

Gomer@Hos.1.3.description: Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, was the wife of the prophet Hosea.
Gomer@Hos.1.3.name: Gomer

Gomorrah@Gen.10.19-Jud.description: Gomorrah was a wicked city in the plain of Jordan that God destroyed with sulfur and fire, along with Sodom, due to their grave sins.
Gomorrah@Gen.10.19-Jud.name: Gomorrah

Goshen@Gen.45.10-Exo.description: Goshen was the region in Egypt where Jacob and his family settled during the time of Joseph, and where the Israelites lived and prospered until the Exodus (<ref="Genesis 45:10; 46:28-29, 34; 47:1, 4, 6, 27; 50:8; Exodus 8:22; 9:26">Genesis 45:10; 46:28-29, 34; 47:1, 4, 6, 27; 50:8; Exodus 8:22; 9:26</ref>).
Goshen@Gen.45.10-Exo.name: Goshen

Goshen@Jos.10.41-.description: Goshen was a town and region in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in the accounts of Joshua's conquests (<ref="Joshua 10:41; 11:16; 15:51">Joshua 10:41; 11:16; 15:51</ref>).
Goshen@Jos.10.41-.name: Goshen

Gozan@2Ki.17.6-Isa.description: Gozan was a region in Mesopotamia where Israelite captives from the northern kingdom were deported by the Assyrians (<ref="2Ki.17.6; 18:11; 19:12; 1Ch.5.26; Isaiah 37:12">2Ki.17.6; 18:11; 19:12; 1Ch.5.26; Isaiah 37:12</ref>).
Gozan@2Ki.17.6-Isa.name: Gozan

Great_Sea@Exo.23.31-Ezk.description: The Great Sea, also known as the Sea of the Philistines, refers to the Mediterranean Sea, which formed the western boundary of the Promised Land (<ref="Numbers 34:6-7; Joshua 1:4; 9:1; 15:12, 47; 23:4; Ezk.47.10, 15, 19-20; 48:28; Exodus 23:31">Numbers 34:6-7; Joshua 1:4; 9:1; 15:12, 47; 23:4; Ezk.47.10, 15, 19-20; 48:28; Exodus 23:31</ref>).
Great_Sea@Exo.23.31-Ezk.name: Great_Sea

Greece@Isa.66.19-Act.description: Greece (Javan), a nation and culture mentioned in both the Old and New Testaments.
Greece@Isa.66.19-Act.name: Greece

Guard_Gate@Neh.12.39.description: The Guard Gate was a gate in Jerusalem's wall, mentioned in <ref="Nehemiah 12:39">Nehemiah 12:39</ref>, likely the same as the Muster Gate near the Temple.
Guard_Gate@Neh.12.39.name: Guard_Gate

Guni@1Ch.5.15.description: Guni, a descendant of Gad, was the father of Abdiel, as mentioned in the genealogy of Gad.
Guni@1Ch.5.15.name: Guni

Guni@Gen.46.24-1Ch.description: Guni was a son of Naphtali and a grandson of Jacob, as listed in the genealogies of Genesis and Numbers.
Guni@Gen.46.24-1Ch.name: Guni

Gur@2Ki.9.27.description: Gur was a place near Ibleam where Ahaziah, king of Judah, was wounded by Jehu's men while fleeing (<ref="2Ki.9.27">2Ki.9.27</ref>).
Gur@2Ki.9.27.name: Gur

Gurbaal@2Ch.26.7.description: Gurbaal was a place inhabited by Arabians, against whom Uzziah, king of Judah, waged war and prevailed (<ref="2Ch.26.7">2Ch.26.7</ref>).
Gurbaal@2Ch.26.7.name: Gurbaal
